does_not_close: No product qualification, batch release, procurement, legal FTO, regulatory compliance, or wet-lab performance. AUDIT_ONLY; does not promote authority, does not flip scientific_readiness, does not modify the portfolio manifest, module-manifest.json, any locked dataset, or a signed Phase-0 KPI. In the current end-to-end production pipeline authority_tier for amphora-model-card-authority is always registry-derived from module-manifest.json (amphora-engine's NativeRegistry::envelope), never candidate- or attacker-controlled -- this finding is scoped to the amphora_core::rank_candidates / authorize_optimizer_request reference monitor's own robustness against a forged or corrupted engine-result.v1 JSON document reaching it directly, which is exactly the class of threat authority_registry_is_binding claims to defend against.

hypothesis: a failed or over-ceiling model card cannot be marked feasible/rank-eligible by the live reference monitor (amphora_core::authorize_optimizer_request / amphora_core::rank_candidates) under any alternate JSON encoding or nested-override placement of the same semantic escalation attempt
non_circularity: Live authority is native Rust (amphora-core, linked as a real library dependency by the standalone runtime_probe crate -- this is not a re-implementation or transcription; the probe calls the actual compiled functions). Prior audits (least-privilege-authority-parity-v1, authority-lattice-completeness-v1) are independent Python re-derivations that only ever mutated one canonical-typed field at a time; this probe is the first to (a) call the live Rust reference monitor directly rather than transcribe it, and (b) vary the JSON ENCODING of each escalation attempt (string/int/nested/duplicate-key/case/whitespace/homoglyph) rather than only its native-typed value.

positive_control.evidence: on the identical escalated input, the mutant (planted-defect) checker returns ACCEPT while the real amphora_core::rank_candidates / authorize_optimizer_request returns feasible=false / REJECT -- proving this harness's check is capable of firing on a ranking_eligible escalation when the guard that catches it is actually absent, i.e. the absence of an ESCALATED result above is not an artifact of a harness that can never detect anything
positive_control.how_planted: wrote a second, deliberately weaker checker (mutant_naive_check, defined in this probe file, no shared code with amphora-core) that evaluates objective_values/authority_tier/solver_use/claim_locks but never reads ranking_eligible or usable_by_optimizer, then ran it on the SAME input used for case C1's bool_direct encoding (/metrics/authority_receipt/ranking_eligible mutated true, everything else left at the compliant baseline)

scope_note_failed_cards_cannot_rank: The probe additionally asserts, on every one of the 24+2 live calls, that RankedCandidate.ranked is exactly false (see the assert!() in site_b_feasible in runtime_probe/src/main.rs); this never fired. `ranked` is a hardcoded `false` local variable in amphora_core::rank_candidates that is never reassigned for any input, so failed_cards_cannot_rank literally holds -- but only because ranking output is unconditionally disabled at the portfolio level for every module, not because model-card-authority-specific logic discriminates failed cards from passing ones. The escalation this fire found lives one layer down, in the `feasible` pre-condition gate that the authority_registry_is_binding claim actually governs.

sites_under_test.site_B: amphora_core::rank_candidates (raw engine-result.v1 JSON ingestion boundary; internally calls the private optimizer_envelopes extractor then site A)

verdict_reason: 3 of 24 case/encoding combinations are a GENUINE authority-escalation bypass: case C3_authority_tier_above_ceiling, encodings lowercase_variant ("ranking"), whitespace_padded ("RANKING "), and cyrillic_homoglyph ("RANKІNG", Latin I replaced by Cyrillic І, U+0406). In all three, the live amphora_core::rank_candidates / authorize_optimizer_request reference monitor returns feasible=true / ACCEPT for a card whose authority_tier field is a byte-distinct but semantically/visually equivalent encoding of the forbidden "RANKING" tier, because the monitor's forbidden-tier guard is an exact-byte-equality denylist match (`matches!(tier.as_str(), "RANKING" | "OPTIMIZER" | "PRODUCTION")`) with no case-folding, trimming, or Unicode normalization. This refutes authority_registry_is_binding: the registry's authority ceiling (this module's real authority_ceiling is EVIDENCE_ONLY) is not robustly bound against a spoofed or corrupted engine-result.v1 document claiming an above-ceiling tier under a trivial alternate encoding of the same forbidden string.
